# PawWork

> PawWork is a free, open-source desktop AI agent for macOS and Windows, built on DeepSeek Harness (DSH) and packaged as a finished product. It handles local files, documents, spreadsheets, research, writing, and code — with no terminal and no subscription. You choose a model provider and supply its API key, and pay that provider directly.

Last updated: 2026-09-01

## About

PawWork brings AI agent work into a native desktop workflow. Users choose a workspace folder, describe a task in plain language, and review the steps, outputs, and generated files before using the result.

PawWork is built for everyday desktop work, not only browser chat or IDE coding. It supports documents, spreadsheets, PDFs, research, writing, code review, debugging, and local file tasks.

PawWork ships no model of its own. On first launch it asks you to pick a provider and paste its API key, and you can switch at any time. Web search is built in and needs no key of its own.

## What PawWork Can Do

- Extract invoice fields from PDFs into a reviewable spreadsheet.
- Summarize CSV data files and create short reports.
- Merge, split, and organize PDF and document files.
- Search the web and collect sources for research tasks.
- Turn notes and attachments into written drafts.
- Inspect code projects, review pull requests, and debug issues with logs and source files.
- Handle Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files locally on your machine.
- Run saved tasks on a cron schedule through Automations, writing results back to the workspace.

## Platforms

- macOS: Apple Silicon and Intel, signed and notarized.
- Windows: x64, currently unsigned installer (SmartScreen may appear on first launch).

## Positioning

PawWork is an open-source alternative to Codex App and Claude Desktop (Cowork). It differentiates with an Apache-2.0 codebase, no subscription of its own, local Office file handling, scheduled automations, and a focus on non-technical users who never open a terminal.

PawWork also differs from the many other DeepSeek Harness desktop applications. Most of those are launchers for developers who already run DSH: they bundle Node, load the official DSH web UI in a window, and expect the user to bring an API key. PawWork instead assembles DSH into a product for people who do not know what DSH is — Office document skills and a Python toolchain are bundled, the shell is native rather than the DSH web UI in a window, and builds are signed for macOS and shipped for Windows. It still asks for a model key, but nothing else. Because the runtime is genuine DSH, community DSH plugins still install and run.

## Built On

PawWork uses DeepSeek Harness (DSH) as its agent runtime, assembled from pinned first-party `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages in a sidecar process rather than by shelling out to a `dsh` CLI. On top of that sit a native Electron shell and a PawWork product layer providing first-run model setup, built-in web search, Automations, and v1 migration. Office support ships as bundled skills for `.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx`, and PDF, executed through a bundled `uv` Python toolchain. PawWork is an independent open-source project and is not affiliated with DeepSeek.
